title: Impact of Immigration on Native Wages

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Instrumental Variables (2SLS)
- Why: Immigrant inflows (x) are likely endogenous to local wage conditions (y); for example, immigrants may choose destinations with better labor markets. Historical settlement patterns (z) provide plausibly exogenous variation in current immigrant inflows via network effects. We use z as an instrument for x.
- Setup:
  - First stage: x = π0 + π1 z + δ' controls + u
  - Second stage: y = β x̂ + γ' controls + e
  - β is the causal effect of immigrant inflow on native wages.
- Key assumptions:
  - Relevance: Cov(z, x | controls) ≠ 0. We will report the first-stage coefficient and robust F-statistic.
  - Exclusion: z affects native wages only through immigrant inflows, conditional on controls (no direct effect on y and no correlation with omitted wage determinants).
  - Exogeneity/Independence: z ⟂ (e, u) conditional on controls.
  - Monotonicity: Historical settlement patterns weakly increase immigrant inflows for all units (no defiers), implying a LATE for areas whose inflows respond to z.
  - SUTVA/no spillovers across units: outcomes in one unit are not directly affected by the instrument in another (acknowledging this can be challenging in spatial contexts; we proceed under this standard assumption).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(AER)        # for ivreg
  library(sandwich)   # for robust vcov
  library(lmtest)     # for coeftest
})

# Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s73_data.csv")

# Helper to pretty-print
prt <- function(x, digits = 4) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)

# 1) OLS (with controls)
ols_mod <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
ols_rob <- coeftest(ols_mod, vcov = vcovHC(ols_mod, type = "HC1"))
beta_ols <- ols_rob["x", "Estimate"]
se_ols   <- ols_rob["x", "Std. Error"]
p_ols    <- ols_rob["x", "Pr(>|t|)"]
ci_ols   <- c(beta_ols - 1.96 * se_ols, beta_ols + 1.96 * se_ols)

# 2) First stage: x ~ z + controls (report relevance)
fs_mod <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
fs_rob <- coeftest(fs_mod, vcov = vcovHC(fs_mod, type = "HC1"))
pi1     <- fs_rob["z", "Estimate"]
se_pi1  <- fs_rob["z", "Std. Error"]
t_pi1   <- pi1 / se_pi1
F_pi1   <- as.numeric(t_pi1^2)
p_pi1   <- fs_rob["z", "Pr(>|t|)"]

# 3) 2SLS IV: y ~ x + controls | z + controls
iv_mod <- AER::ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
iv_rob <- coeftest(iv_mod, vcov = vcovHC(iv_mod, type = "HC1"))
beta_iv <- iv_rob["x", "Estimate"]
se_iv   <- iv_rob["x", "Std. Error"]
p_iv    <- iv_rob["x", "Pr(>|t|)"]
ci_iv   <- c(beta_iv - 1.96 * se_iv, beta_iv + 1.96 * se_iv)

# 4) Reduced form: y ~ z + controls
rf_mod <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)
rf_rob <- coeftest(rf_mod, vcov = vcovHC(rf_mod, type = "HC1"))
beta_rf <- rf_rob["z", "Estimate"]
se_rf   <- rf_rob["z", "Std. Error"]
p_rf    <- rf_rob["z", "Pr(>|t|)"]

# 5) Durbin-Wu-Hausman endogeneity test (classic, from ivreg diagnostics)
iv_sum_diag <- summary(iv_mod, diagnostics = TRUE)$diagnostics
# Extract Wu-Hausman if available
wu_stat <- NA; wu_p <- NA
if (!is.null(iv_sum_diag) && "Wu-Hausman" %in% rownames(iv_sum_diag)) {
  wu_stat <- iv_sum_diag["Wu-Hausman", "statistic"]
  wu_p    <- iv_sum_diag["Wu-Hausman", "p-value"]
}

# 6) Robust control-function endogeneity check (adds first-stage residuals)
fs_resid <- resid(fs_mod)
cf_mod <- lm(y ~ x + controls + fs_resid, data = df)
cf_rob <- coeftest(cf_mod, vcov = vcovHC(cf_mod, type = "HC1"))
cf_p_resid <- cf_rob["fs_resid", "Pr(>|t|)"]

# 7) Robustness: models without controls
ols_nc <- lm(y ~ x, data = df)
ols_nc_rob <- coeftest(ols_nc, vcov = vcovHC(ols_nc, type = "HC1"))
beta_ols_nc <- ols_nc_rob["x", "Estimate"]
se_ols_nc   <- ols_nc_rob["x", "Std. Error"]
p_ols_nc    <- ols_nc_rob["x", "Pr(>|t|)"]

iv_nc <- AER::ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
iv_nc_rob <- coeftest(iv_nc, vcov = vcovHC(iv_nc, type = "HC1"))
beta_iv_nc <- iv_nc_rob["x", "Estimate"]
se_iv_nc   <- iv_nc_rob["x", "Std. Error"]
p_iv_nc    <- iv_nc_rob["x", "Pr(>|t|)"]

# 8) Print clear numerical results
cat("Main results (with controls):\n")
cat("  OLS:     beta_x =", prt(beta_ols), 
    " SE =", prt(se_ols), 
    " 95% CI = [", prt(ci_ols[1]), ",", prt(ci_ols[2]), "]",
    " p =", prt(p_ols), "\n")
cat("  First-stage (x ~ z + controls): coef_z =", prt(pi1),
    " SE =", prt(se_pi1),
    " t =", prt(t_pi1),
    " F =", prt(F_pi1),
    " p =", prt(p_pi1), "\n")
cat("  IV (2SLS): beta_x =", prt(beta_iv), 
    " SE =", prt(se_iv),
    " 95% CI = [", prt(ci_iv[1]), ",", prt(ci_iv[2]), "]",
    " p =", prt(p_iv), "\n")
cat("  Reduced form (y ~ z + controls): coef_z =", prt(beta_rf),
    " SE =", prt(se_rf),
    " p =", prt(p_rf), "\n")

cat("\nEndogeneity diagnostics:\n")
if (!is.na(wu_stat)) {
  cat("  Wu-Hausman (classic): stat =", prt(wu_stat), " p =", prt(wu_p), "\n")
} else {
  cat("  Wu-Hausman: not available from diagnostics\n")
}
cat("  Control-function residual test (robust): p(resid) =", prt(cf_p_resid), "\n")

cat("\nRobustness (no controls):\n")
cat("  OLS (no controls):     beta_x =", prt(beta_ols_nc),
    " SE =", prt(se_ols_nc),
    " p =", prt(p_ols_nc), "\n")
cat("  IV (no controls):      beta_x =", prt(beta_iv_nc),
    " SE =", prt(se_iv_nc),
    " p =", prt(p_iv_nc), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Slightly negative or near zero. Most of the literature finds small average effects of immigration on native wages; substitution in some segments is offset by complementarities and demand effects.
- Magnitude: Modest. A one-unit increase in immigrant inflow (as measured in the dataset) is expected to lower native wages by roughly 0 to -0.2 units, with confidence intervals likely spanning zero in many specifications. The IV estimate should be more negative than OLS if immigrants tend to move to high-wage areas (positive selection bias in OLS). The first-stage should show a positive and statistically significant relationship between historical settlement patterns and current inflows.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use historical settlement patterns as an instrument for immigrant inflow.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The analysis reveals that increased immigrant inflow positively affects native wages.
